answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake, then randomly select a beacon committee to challenge its work against hidden test cases before the identity can earn rewards. Committee members stake too and lose funds if their verdicts diverge from later audits. A sybil operator must therefore immobilize capital for every identity and risk slashing across the canyon of colluding accounts; cheap key generation no longer buys cheap influence. An opal badge can mark identities that survive repeated audits, not replace the stake.
